blocks.text: Osteoporosis is a disease of low bone mass and deteriorated bone structure, leading to fragile bones and fractures from minimal trauma (fragility fractures), most commonly at the spine, hip and wrist. It is diagnosed by a DXA bone density scan (T-score of −2.5 or lower) or by a fragility fracture. Risk factors: age, female sex (especially after menopause), low body weight, smoking, alcohol, long-term steroids, family history, inactivity, rheumatoid arthritis, low calcium and vitamin D [Ref – to verify].
Often silent until a fracture. Signs: height loss, increased thoracic kyphosis, sudden back pain after minor stress (vertebral fracture).
Previous fractures from low trauma; height loss; steroid use; falls; DXA results; current medications; activity level; fear of movement.
Height (compare with previous), wall-to-occiput or rib-to-pelvis distance (possible vertebral fractures), posture, strength, balance, falls risk (Vol 11 Ch 4).

sections.title: G. RED FLAGS AND URGENT CONDITIONS

rows: Sudden severe back pain after minor activity
Hip pain after a fall, unable to weight-bear
Fracture with weight loss, night pain
Back pain with leg weakness or bladder change

steps: **Screen fracture risk** (history, risk tools such as FRAX through the doctor) [Ref – to verify].
**Recent painful vertebral fracture?** Pain management, gentle mobility, posture, progress gradually.
**Stable:** progressive resistance and impact training as tolerated, balance training, education about safe movement.

rows: Squats, deadlift pattern with neutral spine, step-ups, rows, overhead press
2 to 3 times a week, building towards moderate to high intensity under supervision (for example 5 sets of 5 at about 80 to 85% 1RM in selected, trained, supervised patients) [Ref – to verify LIFTMOR]
Heel drops, jumping (low to moderate as tolerated, not in high-fracture-risk patients without supervision)

blocks.text: **Safe movement advice**: avoid repeated, loaded, end-range spinal flexion combined with rotation (for example toe touches, sit-ups with twisting, lifting heavy objects with a rounded back) in people with high fracture risk or previous vertebral fractures [Ref – to verify]. Teach hip hinge and neutral spine.

blocks.label: COMMON STUDENT TRAP
body: Fear of fracture can make patients avoid all exercise. Inactivity weakens bone and muscle and increases fall risk. Properly prescribed exercise is safe and beneficial.

blocks.text: Bracing for acute vertebral fractures may help pain in some cases [Ref – to verify]. Medical treatment (bisphosphonates and others), calcium and vitamin D are decided by doctors.
Strength, balance tests, posture measures, pain, confidence, falls.

items: **Which movements should high-risk patients avoid?** Repeated loaded spinal flexion with rotation.
**Why is resistance training important?** It loads bone, builds muscle and reduces falls risk.
**What does height loss suggest?** Possible vertebral compression fractures.
**Why combine balance training?** Most hip fractures result from falls.

sections.title: Now You Should Be Able To

items: Identify osteoporosis risk and fragility fractures.
Teach safe movement without creating fear.
